images.caption: Bothy at Cragaig, Ulva This bothy is the only roofed building that remains near the abandoned township at Cragaig.  In his book, "The Scottish Islands", Hamish Haswell-Smith's records that in the mid 19th century, the island's new owner, Mr Francis William Clark, evicted many of the island's tenants by burning the roofs of their cottages.

images.caption: Camping at Traigh Bhan In rather windy conditions, we had retreated from Eilean Dioghlum along the south coast of Ulva to a sheltered lagoon and this camping spot. It must be a popular spot for sea kayakers as, despite the evidence of the number of fish boxes littering the coast to suggest that floating debris end up here, the bottom left of the picture shows all the driftwood I managed to find in well over an hour's searching for the best part of a kilometre each way along the shore. Previous visitors had clearly burnt it all !
images.alt: Camping at Traigh Bhan In rather windy conditions, we had retreated from Eilean Dioghlum along the south coast of Ulva to a sheltered lagoon and this camping spot.
